major_concerns: Verifier/modeling mismatch not fully specified (which verifier, supported features, mapping from generated config to verifier model).
Dataset/topology provenance and realism are underspecified (risk of synthetic overfitting).
Repair prompt design and termination rules need concreteness to avoid silent reruns or prompt-tuning bias.
required_design_repairs: Specify exact deterministic verifier/tool (name and version, e.g., Batfish vX or Minesweeper) and its modeling coverage; list properties it will check and failure modes to be excluded.
Provide precise dataset and topology sources (public repo links), inclusion/exclusion rules, and seedable generation procedures for synthetic cases.
Publish frozen prompts, repair-prompt templates, max-iterations policy, retry policy, and exact random seeds in preregistration.
Predefine mapping rules for verifier-detected faults → automated repair prompt inputs so repairs are deterministic given verifier traces.
Add an explicit plan to handle verifier-unmodelable features (exclusion or separate analysis).

major_concerns: Ground-truth vendor configs and dataset licensing/representativeness are insufficiently specified.
Validator coverage for different vendor CLIs may be incomplete (semantic checks vs syntactic parsing).
Prompt-adapter construction (few-shot examples) could leak dataset-specific answers if not preregistered.
required_design_repairs: Provide exact dataset items with public identifiers or a reproducible synthetic generation script; state how vendor diversity is sampled and balanced.
Specify vendor-grammar/syntax validators and semantic-check procedures per vendor (tools, versions, regex/AST definitions).
Freeze and publish the three prompt conditions (vendor-agnostic, vendor-annotated, vendor-adapter few-shot) in the preregistration with seeds for few-shot example selection.
Define actionable-success rubric clearly (what counts as actionable across vendors) and how edit-distance vs semantic correctness are combined.
Pre-register statistical model (mixed-effects formulation) including covariates and planned contrasts.

major_concerns: Simulation fidelity and assumptions (failure models, canary behavior, rollback semantics) are central but underspecified.
Composite metric construction and preregistered threshold (>=0.05 R^2) risk overfitting to simulator; no plan for external validation.
Validators' false-negative measurement depends on oracle definition; needs clear oracle or ground-truth wiring.
required_design_repairs: Describe the simulation engine (codebase or scripts) with public repo link, parameter ranges, and deterministic seeds; include threat model for simulated outages.
Predefine exact composite metric formula or procedure for deriving it (weights, normalization) before model fitting; reserve a held-out validation set or external corpus for assessing generalization.
Specify how validator ground truth is obtained (oracle, golden-config replay, or human annotation) and when validator FN is recorded vs inferred.
Publish deployment protocol parameters (canary %, rollback delay, monitoring windows) and run sensitivity analysis over these parameters as preregistered steps.
Provide cross-validation and model-regularization details, and an a priori plan to avoid tuning the composite to achieve the preregistered R^2 threshold.

major_concerns: Oscillation/divergence detection rules are vague and may misclassify legitimate multi-step repairs.
The decision rule for selecting B* (marginal-gain threshold) is not numerically specified.
Latency and cost assumptions (token pricing, model-latency variability) are unstated, affecting operational recommendations.
required_design_repairs: Define formal oscillation-detection heuristics (e.g., Levenshtein threshold, property-cycle detection) and validate them on pilot traces; publish detection code.
Pre-register the marginal-gain threshold and the statistical procedure for breakpoint analysis that yields B*.
State exact cost/latency accounting assumptions (token cost per model, network round-trip time distribution) and include sensitivity analyses over these parameters.
Provide frozen prompts, critic/verifier implementation/version, and deterministic seeds; publish criteria for legitimate multi-step repairs vs oscillation.
Include a plan to report per-task examples of oscillation and manual adjudication protocol used for edge cases.
